events.text: The ferry-mistress stops her pole mid-stroke. Under the hull, in the pale cloud-water, a ribbon of silver is turning, then a hundred ribbons. The Cloud-Sea eels are running, and they run straight through the fishing lanes, snapping every net they touch.

choices.text: Wade into the shallows of cloud and break the run

ok.log: You stand knee-deep in the cold mist and swat them aside until the run swerves for deeper water. The ferry-mistress lets down a basket of the slowest ones and says nothing, which is thanks.

fail.log: The shoal wraps your legs and drags you under the mist until your lungs remember they are lungs. You surface a long way from the ferry. (-10 health)

choices.text: Mend the nets while the run passes

ok.log: You haul net after net up out of the cloud and knot them back. By dusk the lane is open and the eels are somebody else's worry.

fail.log: The net-lines whip free and take the skin off your palms. (-6 health)

choices.text: Let the run go by

effects.log: You sit on the gunwale and watch the silver pour past for an hour. The mistress shrugs, and poles on.

events.text: A child on the Lantern Isle dock swears the eels spoke to her. Her mother says she was fishing too long in the cloud-glare. But the fishers' lanterns are going out one by one along the quay, and something silver keeps rising to nose at each dead wick.

choices.text: Wait on the dock edge, and meet what rises

ok.log: It rises long as a mast and you meet it with both fists. It slides back under the mist, and the lanterns on the quay are lit again before you have caught your breath.

fail.log: It is faster than a rope and heavier than a door. When you can stand, every lantern on the quay is dark. (-10 health)

choices.text: Light all the wicks again, and keep watch

effects.log: You spend the night walking the quay with a taper. Toward dawn the silver stops rising. The child brings you a rice cake, solemnly, as one guard to another.

events.text: The reed-cutters of the Mist Marsh have not come back from the far beds. Their sickles lie in a line along a trodden path, and at the end of the path, steaming faintly in the cold, a boar the size of a cart is tearing up ghost-reed by the root.

choices.text: Take the path, and take the boar on

ok.log: It charges and you go sideways. After the third pass it is breathing like a bellows, and when it finally goes down the cutters come creeping out of the reeds to claim their sickles.

fail.log: It carries you through four reed-stands before it lets go. The cutters find you in the morning, face down in the muck. (-10 health)

choices.text: Lead it off with a trail of cut reed

ok.log: It follows the sweet-smelling bundles all the way to the far island. The cutters go back to work, whistling.

fail.log: It prefers you to the bundles. (-6 health)

choices.text: Leave it to the marsh

effects.log: You back away. Behind you the tearing and chewing go on, unhurried, as if the marsh had always been its table.

events.text: A boar-sow with a ghost-white hide stands in the mouth of a hollow tree on the marsh road, a litter of striped young squeaking behind her. She has torn up the last two travellers' packs, and has no apparent opinion about you yet.

choices.text: Drive her off the road

ok.log: She gives ground a hand at a time, grunting, and takes her litter into the reeds. The road is clear. You leave a handful of millet at the hollow tree as a kind of apology.

fail.log: She comes through you like a wagon. Her young are not the least impressed. (-10 health)

choices.text: Go around by the long way

effects.log: It takes half a day and two soaked boots. When you pass the hollow tree again a little striped head peers out and then ducks back in.

events.text: The drifting isle has swung close enough to step onto from the ferry rope, and on its crags the white goats stand in rows against the sky. They are watching the rope. They are watching you. One lowers its horns very deliberately and stamps.

choices.text: Step onto the crag and settle it with the herd watching

ok.log: You take the first charge on your forearms and the second on your shoulder, and then the lead goat stops, snorts, and steps aside. The herd parts for you like a curtain.

fail.log: The goat has fought on narrow ledges all its life. You have not. The ledge takes you down and the herd takes the ground. (-10 health)

choices.text: Cross the isle by the goat-paths in single file

ok.log: You learn the rhythm: where they pause, where they leap. At the far edge a herd-master nods you toward the ferry rope.

fail.log: A goat spooks the whole line and you slide to the ledge edge. (-6 health)

choices.text: Cut the rope and wait for another isle

effects.log: You wait three days for the next drift. The goats forget you at once, which is the finest courtesy of the crag.

events.text: Salt-traders of the drifting isle ask a favour as you disembark: the crag goats have been butting down the terrace walls where the tea is grown. They offer a share of the first flush. A very old goat watches from the cliff-top, chewing, with an air of having the better argument.

choices.text: Drive the herd back up the cliff

ok.log: You work them up the cliff face one stubborn pair at a time. The old goat is last, and gives you a look that you will remember.

fail.log: The old goat knows exactly where the footing is bad. You do not. (-10 health)

choices.text: Rebuild the wall higher instead

effects.log: It takes two days and a great many stones. The goats test it, find it good, and wander off with disappointment. The traders send you tea.

choices.text: Tell them the goats were here first

effects.log: The traders do not enjoy hearing it. The old goat lies down on the cliff-top and goes to sleep in the sun.

events.text: The signal-beacon on the Third Isle has gone out, and the watch-sergeant sits on the stair holding a bandaged hand. Overhead a dark bird circles with lightning crawling along its pinions. It stoops again and again at the beacon-bowl. Whatever it wants is in there.

choices.text: Relight the beacon, and take the stoop yourself

ok.log: It folds its wings and falls on you like a spear of weather. You catch the flash on your guard and strike it from the sky. The beacon burns again, brighter than before.

fail.log: The hawk's stoop knocks you off the stair and numbs your arm to the shoulder. The beacon stays dark. (-13 health)

choices.text: Strike the beacon-bowl with a bell so the hawk wheels away

ok.log: The note rings out clear. The hawk shrieks and veers off into the cloud-bank, and the sergeant sags in relief.

fail.log: The bell is wrong for the beacon and the hawk comes down on both of you. (-8 health)

choices.text: Set a bowl of offal on the far wall

effects.log: The hawk takes it with a rattle of thunder and goes. The sergeant looks at you as if you had pulled a trick.

events.text: A courier-skiff crashes into the landing-stage with her pilot half out of the harness and a cracked pennant dragging. "Storm hawk," she gasps, pointing east. "Nest on the ledge-top. It took the post-bird, the relay-stone, the lot." Her eyes ask you to go. Her hands hold out the pennant.

choices.text: Climb to the ledge and take the nest

ok.log: You climb into a gale with its own thunder in it. The hawk falls at the nest rim, and you carry the relay-stone down under your arm to a landing-stage that has started to cheer.

fail.log: The hawk drops you three tiers of cliff, and holds the last word. (-13 health)

choices.text: Carry her to the healer and promise the relay-stone

effects.log: You carry her to the infirmary and promise the stone. By the time you return the hawk has gone, taking the nest with it.

events.text: Fog on the Silver Terrace is common. A fog that walks on four legs is not. The tea-pickers have gathered in the pagoda, and through the open door you see something huge and pale stepping through the bushes without bending a single leaf.

choices.text: Walk into the fog and meet it

ok.log: You find it by the smell of wet moss. It fights as the mist fights, giving where you press and closing where you leave. At last it sits, breathing, and the fog thins.

fail.log: It folds around you like cold wool. You come to in the pagoda with the pickers fanning your face. (-13 health)

choices.text: Offer it honeycomb on a flat stone

ok.log: It eats with great delicacy and then, to the pickers' astonishment, leaves a single pearl of dew on the stone.

fail.log: It eats the honeycomb and the stone with it. (-6 health)

choices.text: Wait in the pagoda until the fog lifts

effects.log: By noon it has gone. The pickers return to the bushes, humming a little too loudly.

events.text: The ferrymen of the Cold Reach have a rule: no lanterns on the fogged water, because the Mist Bear comes to the light. Tonight a novice with a lantern has gone out anyway to fetch a dropped oar. The reach is very quiet, and somewhere out in it, something large breathes in.

choices.text: Row out and put yourself between them

ok.log: It comes out of the fog beside the skiff, and you hold the lantern high and the line low until it loses interest and sinks back. The novice sobs all the way to shore.

fail.log: It knocks the skiff on its side. You are fished from the Reach shivering and the lantern is lost. (-13 health)

choices.text: Row out and douse the lantern in a sack

effects.log: You are a heartbeat too late, but the bear only sniffs at the sack and sinks away. The novice is found weeping in the stern, unharmed.

events.text: The astronomer-monks of the Nine Lamps terrace report that the star-charts have developed a hole: a patch of the night sky where nothing shines. It moves. It is clinging to the terrace rail, long as a doorway, with pale lenses for eyes. It is eating the lamplight.

choices.text: Take the rail, and take the mantis

ok.log: It reaches with forelegs like twin crescent moons. You break the first strike and hold the second, and the lamps flare back to full.

fail.log: It folds your guard like paper. The lamps stay dark half the night. (-13 health)

choices.text: Hang a mirror on the rail, and let it chase its own light

ok.log: It spends a whole night fencing with its own reflection. By dawn it has leapt away into the stars, exhausted.

fail.log: It prefers your light to its own. (-6 health)

choices.text: Let the monks sort out their eclipse

effects.log: You step off the terrace. The next morning they tell you the sky has healed itself.

events.text: A mantis the colour of cold iron stands very still in the middle of the Rope Bridge to Seventh Isle, and no one will cross. A line of pilgrims has formed on either side. Their lanterns throw nervous shadows along its long folded limbs. One of them, an old woman, has taken a seat to wait it out.

choices.text: Walk out onto the bridge and clear it

ok.log: The bridge sways and you fight with your knees bent. At last the mantis topples sideways and flies off into the dark, and the pilgrims cross in a long grateful file.

fail.log: The mantis folds you against the rail. You are helped off the bridge by an old woman who has done this before. (-13 health)

choices.text: Escort the pilgrims around by the long ferry

effects.log: It costs a day but no one is hurt. The old woman thanks you with a charm of knotted thread.

events.text: Frost has begun to crawl up the sides of the Cloud Sea's south wall, an unseasonable rime on a warm sky. Out over the water a shape rolls, gigantic and pale, trailing ice behind it like a wake. A Frost Kun, far from the polar currents, and cold-mad with fever.

choices.text: Board a rimed skiff and meet it on the water

ok.log: The ice cracks under your feet and you break the kun's back-fin with your fists. It dives and goes cold and still, and the rime on the wall begins to run.

fail.log: The cold takes you down to the bone. You are hauled out half frozen, with the skiff in splinters. (-18 health)

choices.text: Kindle a ring of fire-stones on the shore

ok.log: The kun circles the glow for hours before the fever breaks. It drifts away, tame as a cloud.

fail.log: The fire-stones go out under the rime. (-10 health)

choices.text: Warn the southern wall and withdraw

effects.log: You send word to the wall-keepers and fly north. In a week the rime has retreated by itself.

events.text: An ice-wright of the Pale Spire sends a plea: a Frost Kun has been lying across the mouth of the cold-spring that feeds the spire's cisterns, and nothing will move it. Every day the water sinks lower. The kun does not seem to be angry, only vast and in the way.

choices.text: Dislodge the kun from the spring

ok.log: It is heavier than a hill. You work it loose inch by inch with levers of frozen air, and at last it slides free. The spring leaps up behind it, clear as glass.

fail.log: It rolls over you, and the cold is like drowning in milk. (-18 health)

choices.text: Sing it a lullaby until it drifts off on its own

effects.log: You are no singer. It stays an hour to be polite, then drifts, offended or amused, you cannot tell.

events.text: The paddies of the Terrace Isles are drowning, because the Thunder Crane has taken up a stilt in the sluice-gate and will not leave. Every time it shifts its weight lightning forks down the irrigation channels. The water-keepers stand well back with their hands over their ears.

choices.text: Wade in and ask it to step aside

ok.log: It lets you come within two paces and then strikes, beak crackling. You block, sidestep, strike. When it lifts away into the thunderhead the sluice runs clear.

fail.log: It stabs and the whole channel lights up. You are carried out of the paddy twitching. (-18 health)

choices.text: Open the upper sluice and draw the water off

ok.log: The channel runs dry beneath it. Puzzled, the crane takes wing and goes, and the keepers dance on the dike.

fail.log: The sluice wheel bucks and breaks your wrist. (-9 health)

choices.text: Camp on the dike until it tires of the place

effects.log: It stays four days and then, with enormous indifference, flaps away.

events.text: At the Singing Gate of the Eighth Isle a dozen cranes stand in a row, white as paper, and the gate-wardens bow to each. One is not like the others: the smallest, grey-streaked, its feathers crackling at the tips. It turns its eye on you and clacks its beak in a rhythm that sounds almost like a question.

choices.text: Answer the challenge

ok.log: The white cranes part. You fight in the circle of their gaze, and the grey crane yields on the ninth exchange with something very like grace.

fail.log: It strikes first and wins easily, to the polite contempt of the others. (-18 health)

choices.text: Bow to the flock and give the question back

effects.log: You bow. The grey crane clacks once more and folds its wings. The wardens will tell this at supper for a month.

events.text: A lantern-seller found a green scale as large as a platter on the Orchid Isle ferry-steps. Now the whole terrace is quietly watching the old wisteria, which has grown a quarter-mile overnight, its great coils shifting slowly in a wind that is not there. A Jade Cloud Serpent is waking in the roots.

choices.text: Wake it properly, and meet it

ok.log: The wisteria falls apart in your hands and a head the size of a cart-wheel rises out of it. You hold it for nine rounds and at last it lowers itself, shedding blossoms.

fail.log: It coils round you as lightly as a ribbon and squeezes until you cannot breathe. (-18 health)

choices.text: Charm it with a flute from the terrace-end

ok.log: The serpent sways, listening. When the tune ends it dips its head, once, to you, and slides back into the vines.

fail.log: The flute cracks. The serpent is not impressed. (-9 health)

choices.text: Leave the wisteria undisturbed

effects.log: You leave. The serpent sleeps on, and the Orchid Isle takes to calling you the one who tiptoed.

events.text: The jade scales along the Willow Canal are not a decoration. A serpent has been laying itself along the canal bed for a hundred years, and tonight the canal-warden finds the water running backwards. The warden begs you to move it before the whole isle floods.

choices.text: Wade in and shift it

ok.log: You take it by the neck-frill and haul. After a long minute it unwinds, grudgingly, and slides toward the open sky. The canal flows true again.

fail.log: It will not be shifted. The current throws you against the lock. (-18 health)

choices.text: Dredge the canal beside it, to make room

effects.log: Three days of shovelling. The serpent watches you throughout, and on the third night leaves one scale on the lock-gate.

events.text: Something has been hammering at the stone foundation of the Sky-Forge Isle, a boom every few heartbeats, and the masons are afraid to look. You look: a grey horned beast the size of a barn, charging the pylon again and again, horn ringing like struck bronze.

choices.text: Take the charge head on

ok.log: The ground shudders. You take the impact on your braced shoulder and slide a full rod, and when it staggers back you strike with everything you have. It sits, dazed, in the dust.

fail.log: It crumples you against the pylon. The masons carry you to the infirmary. (-18 health)

choices.text: Lay a plate of bronze at the pylon base for it to ring on instead

ok.log: The beast hammers at it with deep satisfaction. By dusk it ambles away, deaf and happy.

fail.log: The plate shifts. The rhino finds the pylon after all. (-10 health)

choices.text: Warn the masons and keep clear

effects.log: The masons shore up the foundation. Within the week the rhino has found a better anvil elsewhere.

events.text: The Smith-Warden of the Anvil Peak offers you a commission. Every century the sky-anvil rhino of the neighbouring crag comes to rub its horn on the forge-stone, and the stone is nearly worn through. If the beast can be driven off, the warden will teach you one lesson of the hammer.

choices.text: Take the commission, and drive the rhino off

ok.log: You strike like the forge-hammer itself. The rhino reels, backs, and wheels away down the crag, and the Warden keeps his word with a long evening at the anvil.

fail.log: The rhino's charge flings you into the quench-trough. (-18 health)

choices.text: Offer the Warden a different bargain: a second stone for the rhino

effects.log: He grumbles, then agrees. Set apart, the stone is rubbed in peace, and the Warden teaches you a lesson anyway.

events.text: The washing on the Windward Terrace flies off the line every dawn, a hundred white shirts ballooning over the cliff, and the washerwomen swear they hear laughter. One morning you catch her at it: a silver fox the colour of fine rain, running along the rail and unhooking pegs with her teeth.

choices.text: Race her along the rail

ok.log: She is faster than breath. But you know the rail, and she does not, and at the turning-post you cut her off and pin her. She laughs in your grip, shaking out a shirt as she goes.

fail.log: She leaps over you and whisks your own sash away. You spend the morning chasing it. (-18 health)

choices.text: Peg every shirt twice, and wait

ok.log: She tries every peg. By evening she gives up with an affronted yip, and the washerwomen clap.

fail.log: She unpegs the lot before you finish. (-6 health)

choices.text: Let her have her game

effects.log: The shirts are found three isles down, clean as snow. The washerwomen are a good deal less cross than they pretend.

events.text: Every kite on the Kite-Mound has been cut loose in the night. The kite-makers gather in sullen groups, and one of them, an old man with a limp, points up into the dark and says: "She's a fox, and she likes the long strings." In the moonlight a streak of silver crosses the mound, tailing ribbons behind her.

choices.text: Chase her over the mound

ok.log: You cut across the ridge, and where the wind turns you turn with it. She skids, tangled in ribbon, and you pin her gently. She looks at you with a bright fox-grin.

fail.log: She runs rings round you and leaves you tangled in your own cord. (-18 health)

choices.text: Fly one great kite as bait

effects.log: She cannot resist it. She spends the dawn dancing under the kite, and the makers retrieve their stock in peace.

events.text: Noon on the Furnace Isle lasts too long. The shadow of the Sunfire Lion has been seen on the brazier terrace, a mane like a halo that never cools. The glass-blowers have fled their workshops and the sand is melting into puddles. It is looking for something warm to lie down in.

choices.text: Walk onto the molten terrace and challenge it

ok.log: The heat is like a hand on your face. You strike through it, wrapped in wet cloth, and the Lion roars, rears, and falls. The glass cools in its puddles, rippling like a held breath.

fail.log: The heat folds you up. You are dragged back with scorched sleeves and a singed brow. (-18 health)

choices.text: Lead it away with a barrow of live coals

ok.log: You walk the coal-barrow along the cliff path for an hour with the Lion padding behind. At the far ledge it lies down in the warm ash and sleeps.

fail.log: The barrow tips and the Lion pounces on the coals, and on you. (-10 health)

choices.text: Wait for the evening chill to move it on

effects.log: Dusk comes, and the Lion goes with it. The glass-blowers tiptoe back to find their furnaces untouched.

events.text: A caravan of pilgrims is camped outside the Sunrise Gate, unable to go in: the great lion lies across the threshold, mane glowing, chewing steadily on a hot iron bar. The gatekeeper has been ordering it off for two days. "It does not take orders," says the gatekeeper, "from anyone. It only takes bars."

choices.text: Show the lion who the gate belongs to

ok.log: You step onto the threshold and speak the one word of the gate. The lion regards you, yawns, and finally rises to meet you. When it falls it leaves one coal-bright hair on the step.

fail.log: The lion rises and the gate is full of its heat. You are tossed through the pilgrims. (-18 health)

choices.text: Feed it another bar from the smithy

effects.log: It eats, burps a small flame, and gets up with a stretch. The pilgrims go in under its gaze, humbled.

events.text: The Cloud-Tide is out, and the fisherfolk of the Low Isles are meant to be harvesting the pearl-mist. But the tide has a head, as if the sea had grown teeth, and scaled coils are stirring out beyond the breakers, ploughing the cloud into foam. A Cloud-Tide Drake, in the wrong season.

choices.text: Go out on the foam and meet it

ok.log: You fight standing on a plank, the drake coiling round you in cold spray. At last you wrestle its head down onto the shingle, and the tide, abruptly, relaxes.

fail.log: The drake rolls and pulls you under. You are fished out among the empty pearl-baskets. (-18 health)

choices.text: Lay a string of lanterns to guide it back to deep water

ok.log: It follows the lights out beyond the breakers and sinks, trailing one long glistening wake.

fail.log: The lanterns are swamped. (-9 health)

choices.text: Warn the fisherfolk to keep inland

effects.log: They stay home that tide. The drake stirs and sulks and goes in the end, leaving the pearl-mist untouched.

events.text: A girl at the Dragon-Mouth Stairs says that the tide drake is her friend. She has fed it fish-heads for a year. Now it has a cut on its flank, and the river-wardens want it gone before it reaches the pilgrim channel. She stands between you and the water with her chin up.

choices.text: Do the wardens' work, and drive it off

ok.log: You fight carefully, with the girl's eyes burning into your back. It retreats down the stairs into the deep, and she does not speak to you for a year.

fail.log: It sweeps you down the stairs, and the girl drags you out by the collar, furious. (-18 health)

choices.text: Dress the cut, and send it home

effects.log: You daub its flank with salve while the girl holds its head. The drake glides away. The wardens grumble, but the stairs stay open.

events.text: Where the Cloud Sea runs deepest, the sky itself seems to draw breath. Beneath your skiff a shape begins to rise: mile-long, slate-blue, scarred by ten thousand storms, with an eye as big as a lake. The Old Whale of the Cloud Sea. Fishermen say it has been here since before the isles drifted. It has come up to look at you.

choices.text: Ask the Old Whale for the honour of a bout

ok.log: You fight on its back in a river of mist, and in the end it lowers itself beneath you and sings one long note that rings in the isles for a hundred years.

fail.log: The whale is gentle with you, by its standards. You wake a day later on a shore, alive and humbled, and it is gone. (-35 health)

choices.text: Lower your head and let it pass

effects.log: Its shadow passes over you for the length of a prayer. The cloud-fishers will tell this tale for generations.

events.text: Every hundred years the Old Whale rises under the Harvest Isle. The elder fisherfolk gather on the sea-wall with offerings of fruit and rice, the young ones whispering. As it breaches, a wave of cloud crests over the wall. Its great eye turns, finds you among the crowd, and does not move on.

choices.text: Step forward and ask it for a bout

ok.log: You fight across the leaping spray and the elders hold their breath. It dips its vast head to you at the end, and the Harvest Isle sings your name for a month.

fail.log: It lifts you gently out of the sea and sets you down on the wall, and goes. The elders are very kind about it. (-35 health)

choices.text: Add your own offering to the pile and bow

effects.log: You lay a bowl of rice on the wall. The whale blinks, once, and sinks. The cloud settles over the sea like a closing hand.

events.text: The sleepers of Mongsa's marches have stopped waking. Pilgrims lie in rows in the dreaming-hall, smiling, while overhead in the lamplight a cloud of grey moths turns and turns, scattering a fine pale dust. They are feeding. The dream-priests, drowsy themselves, beg you to put them out.

choices.text: Break up the swarm with a wind of your own

ok.log: You whirl through the hall like a storm. The moths scatter, flutter, thin. One by one the sleepers sit up, blinking, to find a god among the lamps.

fail.log: The dust gets in your eyes. You wake an hour later among the sleepers, with a pillow under your head. (-10 health)

choices.text: Extinguish every lamp but one

ok.log: The moths converge on the last flame. You snuff it too, and the swarm dissolves into the darkness.

fail.log: The one lamp you leave gutters. The moths settle on you. (-6 health)

choices.text: Leave the sleepers to their rest

effects.log: You leave the hall to its murmuring. The moths are gone by morning, and no one remembers the dream they wanted.

events.text: A child in the dream-market brings you a jar with a single dream-moth in it. She found it in her mother's hair. The mother has not woken in six days. The child is not crying. She holds the jar out at arm's length, as if she were bringing you a fever.

choices.text: Take the jar, and hunt the rest of the swarm

ok.log: You follow the dust-trail to a cellar in the old quarter, where a hundred moths hang like grey fruit. You break them with a clap of your palms, and the mother wakes, asking for tea.

fail.log: The swarm turns on you and the dust falls like snow. You sleep through a whole festival. (-10 health)

choices.text: Hold the jar to the mother's ear and call the moth back

effects.log: The moth beats against the glass, and the mother stirs. It is a small mercy and a clumsy one. She wakes with only half her dream.

events.text: The fields of Pungnyeon are meant to be abundant, and the farmers are meant to be grateful. This year a boar the size of a threshing cart has been coming down from the hills at night and eating the first harvest. The farmers, sweating, have made a small offering to you: the choice of first cut.

choices.text: Wait in the barley and take the boar

ok.log: It comes out of the dark snorting, tusks like sickles. You stop it with a shoulder and put it down, and in the morning the farmers kneel in the stubble.

fail.log: It scores a line through the barley, and through you. You are carried to the village with a field of crushed ears behind you. (-10 health)

choices.text: Set out a sack of sweet peas away from the field

ok.log: The boar goes for the peas. The barley is spared, and you are given a basket of figs as thanks.

fail.log: The boar prefers both. (-6 health)

choices.text: Teach the farmers a better fence

effects.log: It takes a week and a great deal of rope. The boar tries the new fence once and gives up.

events.text: An old sow of the harvest-herd stands in the road to the granary, the mark of the Pungnyeon shrine on her ear. She is thin and ragged and has been fed by the priests for years. Now the priests are dead or gone, and she has come to see what the new god will do. The farmers peer from the barn.

choices.text: Treat her as a pest and drive her off

ok.log: She bolts, snorting, and does not return. The farmers cheer thinly and look away.

fail.log: She has more weight than you gave her credit for. You are rolled in the dust. (-10 health)

choices.text: Give her the old offering and promise better

effects.log: She eats from your hand, and trots back to the hills without a backward look.

events.text: At the grey edge of Haeryong's shallows the shore-folk keep their boats pulled high, because the Reef Hounds hunt on the tide. They look like seals, with the heads of hounds, and they come in packs. Tonight the ebb is long, and a whole pack is working the sandbars, barking in the dark.

choices.text: Meet the pack on the sandbar

ok.log: You fight in water to your knees, back to the tide-post. The pack is clever, but you are patient. By dawn the hounds are gone and the boats are safe.

fail.log: They circle in the shallows until you are dizzy, and then nip all at once. (-10 health)

choices.text: Row out and lure the leader to deep water with a net of mackerel

ok.log: The leader follows the mackerel out past the bar. The pack follows the leader. By morning the shore is silent.

fail.log: The net tangles in the oars. (-6 health)

choices.text: Raise the boats higher on the shingle and wait

effects.log: The pack barks all night and takes nothing. In the morning the tide has turned, and so have they.

events.text: A fisherman's widow in the shallows shows you a boat with its ropes chewed through. "They are not bad things," she says. "They are hungry. The reef was richer when my husband was young." She holds out her hand, palm up, as though asking you to decide whether she is right.

choices.text: Drive the pack from her cove

ok.log: The pack falls back before you, yelping. The widow thanks you gravely and says, as you go, that they will be back.

fail.log: The hounds know this water. They harry you into the surf and leave. (-10 health)

choices.text: Seed the shallows with shellfish and leave a net of fish

effects.log: The hounds eat, and eat, and settle. The widow takes the work as a blessing and names a child for you.

events.text: On the high pastures of Noegong, the flocks have stopped climbing. Every night something strikes the ridge with a crack that rolls down the valley, and in the morning another shepherd is missing one ewe. The shepherds have seen it: a ram, black-fleeced, horns wreathed in blue sparks.

choices.text: Climb the ridge and meet the ram

ok.log: The ram charges across the scree in a crash of thunder. You catch the horns, and for a moment the whole ridge lights up. Then it kneels.

fail.log: The ram's charge lifts you off the crag and sets you down half stunned in the gully. (-13 health)

choices.text: Ground the flock-pen with a copper rod

ok.log: The next strike runs harmlessly into the earth. The ram snorts, puzzled, and wanders away.

fail.log: The rod does nothing, and the ram is not fooled. (-8 health)

choices.text: Move the flock to the lower pasture for the season

effects.log: It takes a week to coax the sheep down. The shepherds grumble but the strikes stop.

events.text: A boy brings you a shard of black horn found at the foot of the ridge. It still hums faintly. The ram has been to the shrine of Noegong at the peak, he says, and has not come back. The boy's whole village is gathered at the foot of the slope, looking up.

choices.text: Take the shard up the mountain

ok.log: You climb through a roaring storm and find the ram standing alone at the cold altar. You fight until the lightning is spent, and it yields, steaming.

fail.log: The ram strikes you off the altar steps. (-13 health)

choices.text: Carry the shard to the shrine and leave it on the altar

effects.log: The thunder stops that night. No one sees the ram again, but in the morning the shard is gone.

events.text: The pilgrim road up the slope of Daeak has been closed for a month. A Mountain Ape sits in the middle of it, grey as the stone, chewing a root and watching the road with an expression of deep suspicion. It throws boulders at anyone who comes within a hundred paces.

choices.text: Walk up the road and settle it

ok.log: You catch its boulder on your shoulder and bring it down in front of the ape. It stares at the boulder, then at you, and after a long time rises and moves aside.

fail.log: The ape catches you by the leg and throws you back down the road. (-13 health)

choices.text: Climb the cliff beside the road and approach from behind

ok.log: You come over the rim silently, and the ape, startled, bolts. The pilgrims climb in a long line, whispering thanks.

fail.log: The ape sees you coming and sends a boulder after you. (-9 health)

choices.text: Leave a basket of fruit at a safe distance

effects.log: It sniffs the basket from afar. By nightfall the road is open and the basket is empty.

events.text: An old ape of Daeak sits in the doorway of a ruined shrine, picking at the hem of a pilgrim's robe left on the step. She does not move when you approach. The robe is not hers. An acolyte whispers that the ape is the one who hurt the last priest, and that the temple wants her gone.

choices.text: Do the temple's bidding

ok.log: She stands, slowly, and you fight carefully in the doorway. She goes down at last and does not rise. You wonder if the temple was right.

fail.log: She sets you back on the step with one blow. (-13 health)

choices.text: Sit beside her and hear the acolyte out again

effects.log: The acolyte stumbles, then admits the priest died of old age. The ape picks at the robe, and does not look up.

events.text: The kilns of Hwarin have been burning low since the equinox. A hearth salamander has crawled into the main flue and settled in the bank of coals, red as a burnt coin, tail dangling out into the cold. The potters say it is not unfriendly. They say it is just very large.

choices.text: Pull it from the flue

ok.log: You haul it out by the tail in a shower of ash. It hisses and sulks, and when you set it on the cold stone it flickers and fades to a dull ember-glow.

fail.log: It sears your palms, and you let go. The flue stays blocked. (-13 health)

choices.text: Coax it out with a lump of live charcoal

ok.log: It follows the charcoal like a puppy. The kiln roars back to life behind it.

fail.log: It eats the charcoal, and then your sleeve. (-6 health)

choices.text: Let the kiln burn low this season

effects.log: The potters make do. By midwinter the newt has moved on to a warmer hearth, and the kiln roars back.

events.text: In the glaze-hall a child holds up a clay pot that glows from the inside. A newt as long as her arm sits in it, tail curled, blinking at the light. "Mine," she says. Her father, behind her, has the fixed smile of someone who knows how bad the next bit will be.

choices.text: Take the newt from her, for the good of the hall

ok.log: It leaps and you catch it. The child bursts into furious tears. The glaze-master thanks you thinly.

fail.log: It spits a fiery pellet and the child shrieks with joy. (-13 health)

choices.text: Let the child keep her friend

effects.log: The glaze-master sighs. The pot glows on the shelf all winter, and the pots fired beside it come out with a gold shimmer.

events.text: On the high ridge between domains, snow has begun to fall in summer. A great white stag stands in the middle of the pass, antlers branching into the clouds, frost spreading from its hooves in lacy ferns. The pilgrims turn back. It stares at them as they go, and then at you.

choices.text: Climb to the ridge and meet the stag

ok.log: You fight across a field of ice that rings like glass, and at last you catch its antlers. It looks into your eyes, and bows its head.

fail.log: The cold takes you in a mantle of white. You wake in a drift, alive, with frost in your hair. (-18 health)

choices.text: Light a ring of fire on the ridge to turn it back

ok.log: It circles the glow, then trots away northwards. The summer returns to the pass.

fail.log: The flames freeze to a crust. (-10 health)

choices.text: Wait on the near slope until it passes

effects.log: The snow lifts by dawn. The pilgrims cross the ridge, shaking their heads.

events.text: A hunter's horn on the high ridge: the god of the pass, who has been gone a thousand years, supposedly rides a frost stag on the first night of winter. The villagers set out a bowl of milk for him. Tonight the bowl is frozen to the stone, and there is a stag at the village edge, riderless.

choices.text: Step out and challenge the empty stag

ok.log: You fight across the village green with the whole hamlet watching from behind their shutters. It yields, trembling, as the first snow falls.

fail.log: The stag lowers its antlers and sends you through the milk-bowl. Nobody dares laugh. (-18 health)

choices.text: Pour a fresh bowl of milk and wait

effects.log: The stag drinks. When it lifts its head it looks almost like a god, then it is only a stag. It goes back to the ridge before the dawn.

events.text: A wyrm of clouds has taken the old watchtower of the border domain for its nest, its coils wound round the stone, lightning flickering in its throat. The watch has fled. It blocks the only road between two shrines. A lone postman waits at its foot, holding an envelope.

choices.text: Climb the tower and have it out

ok.log: You climb through a gale of its making. At the summit, in the roar of thunder, you grapple it round the throat. It goes limp, and the cloud around the tower drifts apart.

fail.log: The wyrm coils you to the balustrade and shakes you. You come to at the foot of the tower. (-18 health)

choices.text: Send the postman through while you hold its eye

ok.log: It watches you the whole time. The postman scurries through. When he is safely gone, the wyrm lowers its head, bored.

fail.log: It notices the postman after all. (-9 health)

choices.text: Take the long road around the domain

effects.log: The detour is two weeks, wet and dull. But the wyrm leaves in its own time.

events.text: Every night this month a hurricane has circled one patch of coast, and every night the village there sleeps through it. The village elders say that the wyrm lives in it, and that it is only looking for a place to sleep. Tonight the hurricane has stopped, and a sound like a great cat purring comes from the beach.

choices.text: Step into the stillness and wake it

ok.log: It is startled awake, and thunders. You fight it down the whole beach in a sheet of rain, and when it is done it lies curled on the strand and the coast is quiet.

fail.log: It rises like the whole sky and flings you out to sea. (-18 health)

choices.text: Fetch the elders, and let them make an offering

effects.log: The offering is a bowl of fried fish, left on the sand. The wyrm eats, sighs, and rises, trailing a small friendly storm. It does not come back.

events.text: The sacred grove of Saengmo is overgrowing the road. Every day a tree sprouts on the pilgrim path, and a tortoise the size of a hill is lumbering slowly through the glades, shedding saplings from its back. The grove-keepers have asked you to see it off before the road disappears.

choices.text: Block its path and test its strength

ok.log: It is immovable at first, and then, abruptly, not. You push the great shell back from the road, and it turns with infinite slowness and goes.

fail.log: It rolls over you like a landslide. (-18 health)

choices.text: Lead it away with a trail of lettuce

ok.log: It follows, eating at the pace of a glacier. By evening you have it a mile from the road.

fail.log: It prefers the grove. (-8 health)

choices.text: Let the grove grow

effects.log: The pilgrims make a new road around the grove, and some say it is the better.

events.text: An old woman in the forest hut says the moss tortoise carried her husband's ashes down to the sea once, long ago. "It would not take payment," she says. "I thought you might like to know before you decide what to do with it." The great shell is just visible through the trees.

choices.text: Go and test it all the same

ok.log: It lets you strike a while, and then it speaks, a low rumble, thanking you for the exercise. It slides away into the trees.

fail.log: The shell turns aside every blow and then knocks you flat. (-18 health)

choices.text: Go and thank it instead

effects.log: You find it in a clearing. It lowers its head to be scratched. You leave a ribbon on its shell.

events.text: The terraces of Daeak are crumbling. Every night a Stone Bull, grey as the cliff it was carved from, comes down the mountain and charges the retaining walls, horns sparking, and the farmers wake to find another stairway of fields washed away. The bull has horns of flint.

choices.text: Stand in the gap and turn it

ok.log: It hits you with the weight of a falling boulder. You hold, and strike, and strike again, until the bull rocks back onto its haunches and the terraces are saved.

fail.log: It lifts you clean off your feet and into the wall. (-18 health)

choices.text: Build a decoy wall of loose stones to draw it away

ok.log: It charges the false wall with satisfaction. By dawn it has demolished it, and gone.

fail.log: It ignores the decoy. (-10 health)

choices.text: Wait for the bull to tire itself out

effects.log: It does, three nights later. It plods back up the mountain, and the terraces hold.

events.text: At the quarry-shrine a bull of grey granite stands at the altar, as it has for a thousand years. Lately it has been shifting. A sculptor carving the shrine's pillar swears it blinked at him. When you come in, the stone shoulder rolls, and the eyes open, and a low rumble fills the shrine.

choices.text: Test the stone bull in the shrine

ok.log: The shrine rings with your blows. The bull submits at last and goes still, and the sculptor begins, shakily, to chip a new pillar.

fail.log: It rolls over you like a tide of rock. (-18 health)

choices.text: Bow to it as to an old guardian

effects.log: The bull settles on its haunches. The sculptor, wide-eyed, begins carving it a pedestal.

events.text: The ridge-roads of Horang's mountains were safe for centuries. Now a tiger the colour of cloud-shadow stalks the passes, and where it walks the grass lies flat in a long streak. Merchants go in groups of fifty. Even then a pack-mule goes missing, and no one hears a thing.

choices.text: Lie in wait on the ridge and take it

ok.log: It passes you on the wind, and you strike where the air bends. The tiger rolls, rises, and you wrestle in the long grass until it lies still.

fail.log: It strikes and is gone. You find yourself ten paces away with a torn cloak. (-18 health)

choices.text: Follow the flattened grass and read where it will pass

ok.log: You get ahead of it and wait. When it comes, you do not strike, only stand. It looks at you, and turns aside.

fail.log: It reads you first. (-9 health)

choices.text: Escort the next caravan and stay out of the way

effects.log: The tiger watches the caravan from the ridge. Nothing is taken. The merchants swear by you.

events.text: A hunter of Horang's slopes shows you a pelt of cloud-grey fur, striped like wind on water. "I took this from a tiger two winters past," he says, "and since then, it has haunted my dreams. Now I think it follows me." On the ridge above his house, in the dusk, something large is pacing.

choices.text: Face the tiger's grief

ok.log: It comes down the slope with a roar like a gust. You meet it, hold it, and it sags in your grip, heavy with sorrow. The hunter sobs quietly.

fail.log: It sweeps you aside and goes straight for the hunter's door. (-18 health)

choices.text: Bury the pelt on the ridge

effects.log: You carry the pelt up in the dark and bury it under a cairn. The pacing stops. In the morning there is a single track in the frost, leading away.

events.text: A shadow like a burning kite passes across the summer fields of the Scorching Domain, and the crops catch alight where it falls. The villagers stamp out fires all night. High above, huge and red-gold, circles an Ember Roc, and the heat of its wings makes the sky ripple.

choices.text: Wait in an open field and meet its stoop

ok.log: It comes down like a falling furnace. You take its talons on your guard, and send it spinning out into the sky. Where it falls the fires go out.

fail.log: It sets your sleeves alight and takes the field. (-18 health)

choices.text: Soak the fields with water and keep the villagers inside

ok.log: The roc circles three times and flies on. The fields stay green.

fail.log: The flames leap the soaked ground. (-10 health)

choices.text: Let the roc pass, and pray for rain

effects.log: It passes. The rain does not come, but the fires die on their own.

events.text: The nest of the Ember Roc sits on a spire of black glass. Pilgrims climb it once a generation, to ask for the god's favour, and are never seen again. Today a young priest of Hwarin has asked you to go in her place, because her teacher has died, and no one else will.

choices.text: Climb the spire and face the roc

ok.log: You climb through the glow and the roc rises in front of you with a scream. The fight takes all day and ends with a nod. The priest weeps with relief at the foot.

fail.log: The roc scorches the spire and you with it. You come down on a ledge, dazed. (-18 health)

choices.text: Carry the priest's offering up and leave it unguarded

effects.log: You leave a bowl of honeyed rice at the nest-rim and retreat. It accepts, and does not trouble you again.

events.text: The deep wells of Haeryong's temple go down a thousand fathoms, and the priests who draw water have begun to hear singing from them. Tonight the well-rope comes up dripping green, and a coil as thick as a barrel appears at the rim, scales slick, a great head following. The priests scatter.

choices.text: Grip the coil and wrestle it back down

ok.log: It is a long cold fight, and you hold the rim against the whole weight of the sea. At last the serpent slips down into the dark, and the priests re-seal the well.

fail.log: It pulls you halfway over the rim and holds you there until the priests haul you free. (-18 health)

choices.text: Drop a lantern down the shaft and call it back

ok.log: It watches the lantern descend, then follows, slow as a tide. The well is quiet again.

fail.log: The lantern goes out, and the serpent does not. (-9 health)

choices.text: Seal the well with a stone slab and wait

effects.log: It takes four men to drag the slab. The singing stops, eventually.

events.text: A fisherwoman of the northern shallows drops her catch at your feet, trembling. She saw it from the shore: a snake as long as a river rising out of the deep, circling a fishing boat, pulling the boat down gently, almost kindly. The boat's three crewmen are still on it, calling out.

choices.text: Wade out and take the serpent on

ok.log: You fight in water to your chest, the crew shouting from the bow. At last the serpent releases the boat, and sinks.

fail.log: It drags you under until the crew pull you out by the hair. (-18 health)

choices.text: Swim out with a rope and bring the crew back by hand

effects.log: The serpent lets you. It watches you do it, and you are never sure whether it was permission or contempt.

events.text: A domain fell here, ages ago. Its god is dust and its temples are weeds, and nothing lives among the broken pillars. But on the empty altar, vast and patient, lies a shape you do not recognise: the First Beast of the fallen domain, who watched it end and could not leave. Its eye opens. It knows you.

choices.text: Ask the First Beast for the honour of a bout

ok.log: You fight across the ruins, among the pillars, and at the end it lowers itself and gives you one low call, the last of its kind. The sky above the ruins goes quiet.

fail.log: It is gentle with you, by its standards. You wake a day later among the weeds, alive and humbled, and it is gone. (-35 health)

choices.text: Kneel among the pillars and let it keep its vigil

effects.log: It watches you for a long moment, then closes its eye. You leave the ruin undisturbed. The domain will not forget.

events.text: A dying beast lies at the foot of the ruined stair, ribs standing out like a ship's frame. It was the first of its domain, say the priests, born before the temples. Now it waits at the stair for a god that will never come. It lifts its heavy head and looks at you, and your title does not seem to matter to it at all.

choices.text: Offer it the dignity of a bout

ok.log: It rises for you, magnificent for one moment. You fight under the broken arch, and when it lies down again it is at peace, and the stair is quiet.

fail.log: It rises, and strikes once, and the wind of it throws you down the stair. When you wake it has settled back to wait. (-35 health)

choices.text: Sit with it until evening

effects.log: You sit on the stair through a long, cold sunset. It does not stir. At dusk you rise, bow, and go. A single bell rings somewhere in the dark.

events.text: The shepherds of the north ridge have lost eleven lambs this month. At dusk you see why: a grey line of wolves moving down the scree in single file, thin as winter, intent. This world is young, and its wolves have not yet learned to fear anything with two legs.

choices.text: Hold the ridge-path with a staff

ok.log: You hold the narrow place until the leader tires of testing you. The pack lopes away into the dusk, and the shepherds bring you a cheese the size of a wheel.

fail.log: They find the gap in your guard in the first minute. You limp back to the sheepfold, torn and humbled. (-10 health)

choices.text: Build a ring of brush fires around the fold

ok.log: The wolves circle all night, and in the morning there is not a lamb missing.

fail.log: The brush catches your sleeve. (-6 health)

choices.text: Let the shepherds hold the fold themselves

effects.log: You tell them where to put the dogs and ride on. The wolves take one lamb, and the village complains for a month.

events.text: A boy runs up a lane shouting that wolves have cornered his sister in the old hay-barn. When you get there the pack sits in a ring outside, patient, tongues lolling, while a small voice inside sings a lullaby to keep its courage up. The wolves seem to be listening.

choices.text: Walk into the ring and break it

ok.log: The ring parts, snarling, and closes again as you pass. You win by waiting for the leader's hesitation, and drive the pack down the lane.

fail.log: The leader is no fool. It brings you to the ground and keeps you there. (-10 health)

choices.text: Sing the second verse of the lullaby, and walk in

effects.log: The wolves tilt their heads. You walk through the ring and take the girl out by the hand, and nobody stops you.

events.text: Your world's marsh breeds fat boars, and this year one has taken the causeway between two villages for its own. It sits in the middle of the planks, steaming gently, and any cart that tries to pass is rammed off into the reeds. The carters have started calling it the Toll-Keeper.

choices.text: Fight the Toll-Keeper on the planks

ok.log: You catch it at the gap in the rail and push, and it goes into the reeds with a splash that carries to the next village. The carters raise a cheer.

fail.log: It rams you into the marsh. You emerge reeking, to the delight of the carters. (-10 health)

choices.text: Bait it off the causeway with turnips

ok.log: It trots after the turnips like a lamb. The causeway is clear by supper.

fail.log: It takes the turnips and keeps the road. (-6 health)

choices.text: Ford the marsh by hand instead

effects.log: It takes the whole afternoon and ruins your boots, but nobody gets rammed.

events.text: A marsh boar has dug up the vegetable garden of the widow at the willow cottage, root by root. She stands at the gate with a ladle, grim. "I've asked it nicely," she says. "I've asked it not nicely. I think it would like to be fought." She looks at you hopefully.

choices.text: Oblige the boar

ok.log: The boar charges with something almost like joy. You tumble it over the garden wall, and the widow serves you pickled cabbage until you cannot move.

fail.log: The boar flattens you into the bean rows, and the widow clucks sympathetically. (-10 health)

choices.text: Fence the garden with stakes and call it finished

effects.log: The widow watches you work, not entirely satisfied. The boar takes to digging next door.

events.text: A hill bear has woken a month too early, thin and ill-tempered, and it has taken to raiding the honey-boxes behind the bee-keeper's hut. She stands in the lane with a hive-smoker in her hand and the look of someone whose patience is at an end.

choices.text: Meet the bear at the honey-boxes

ok.log: It rises on its hind legs with a roar, and you grapple it among the toppled boxes. When it drops, it limps off into the hills without looking back.

fail.log: The bear has a paw like a shovel. You are carried to the hut with a bee in each ear. (-10 health)

choices.text: Move the boxes up into the loft

ok.log: It takes all night. The bear returns at dawn to find an empty yard, and lumbers away muttering.

fail.log: The first box slips and splits. (-6 health)

choices.text: Leave a pot of honey at the forest edge

effects.log: It takes the pot. The bee-keeper scowls at you, then offers you a spoonful.

events.text: The lane-children have found a bear cub asleep under the old plum tree, and the mother is somewhere near. The children are cooing. You can hear the mother, in the wood, working her way down to the lane, and she is not cooing.

choices.text: Stand between the cub and the mother

ok.log: She arrives in a rush. You hold her until she realises you are not a threat to the cub, and she gathers it up and leaves. The children are subdued.

fail.log: She does not stop to think. You are bundled into the plum tree. (-10 health)

choices.text: Chivvy the children home and leave the cub to the mother

effects.log: You herd the children away in a long straggling line. Behind you a deep grunt, a soft whimper, and then silence.

events.text: The iron elk of your world's high moor have antlers like wrought railings, and in the rutting season they take the moor road for their own. This autumn the road has not reopened. A stag stands in the middle of it, eight points on a side, its breath steaming. Traders wait at both ends, muttering.

choices.text: Meet the stag with your back to a boulder

ok.log: It lowers its antlers, rings them against the stones, and charges. You catch the beam and bear it aside. After four charges it turns and goes, trailing steam.

fail.log: The elk throws you into a bank of heather and stands over you, breathing. (-13 health)

choices.text: Ring a hand-bell to herd it off the road

ok.log: It tosses its head, snorts, and leaves the road at an unhurried walk.

fail.log: The bell only angers it. (-8 health)

choices.text: Wait for the rut to end

effects.log: The stag stays for four days. When it goes, the road is thick with antler-scrapes.

events.text: A smith at the moor-forge offers you a trade: iron from the old seam, if you will bring him an antler of the iron elk. They shed one every autumn, he says, but only when they feel like it. He nods toward the hillside, where a dark shape is pacing the skyline.

choices.text: Go and try for the antler

ok.log: You take it by the beam and wrestle it down, and at last the antler comes away in your hands. The elk gets up, looking bewildered, and trots into the mist.

fail.log: The elk does not oblige. You are chased across three streams. (-13 health)

choices.text: Climb the slope and wait for it to shed

effects.log: It does, eventually, three days later. The smith takes the antler with reverence and gives you what he promised.

events.text: The night-ferry runs on lamplight, and lately the lamps have been going out. Something with enormous round eyes sits on the ferry-post, wings folded, and it has a glow in its chest like a lantern. The ferryman will not row until it goes. It will not go until the lamps are out.

choices.text: Drive the owl from the post

ok.log: You come at it on the dark water. It rises with an enormous soft beat of wings, flashing light in your eyes, and you strike it down onto the post. It stops glowing, grumpy.

fail.log: It dazzles you with its glow, and you pitch into the river. (-13 health)

choices.text: Snuff the lamps and wait it out

ok.log: It blinks, annoyed, and flaps off. The ferryman lights the lamps again, one by one.

fail.log: In the dark it knocks you off the jetty. (-7 health)

choices.text: Take the day ferry instead

effects.log: You wait for the sun. The owl has gone by dawn, and the night ferry resumes.

events.text: Children claim the owl on the schoolhouse roof has been speaking. "It says the same thing every night," says a small girl. "It says, 'put out the light.'" The teacher shushes her, but she looks uneasy. On the roof-ridge a pair of bright round eyes blink slowly down at the yard.

choices.text: Climb up and put out its light

ok.log: You ascend to the ridge and meet it eye to eye. It dims at last, mortified, and flies into the pines.

fail.log: It hisses, spreads its wings, and sends you tumbling down the slates. (-13 health)

choices.text: Put out the lamps in the schoolhouse and see what it does

effects.log: The owl watches the dark windows for a while, then glides away. The girl nods, vindicated.

events.text: The thorn-hedge of the farm road has grown arms. A cat the size of a calf slinks along the hedge-bottom, her coat knotted with burrs and briars, and the harvesters say she hunts at dusk. She has taken three geese and a goat, and she watches the farmhouse windows with a patient, level gaze.

choices.text: Take the cat in the open stubble

ok.log: You catch her midleap and bear her down onto the stubble. She goes slack, glaring, and slinks away into the hedge, shedding briars.

fail.log: She takes your sleeve and half your shoulder with it. (-13 health)

choices.text: Set a goose-trap in the lane

ok.log: The cat takes the bait and the net closes on her. She yowls, then eats the goose quietly, and goes.

fail.log: She steals the goose and the net. (-6 health)

choices.text: Cut a gap in the hedge for her to leave by

effects.log: You spend an afternoon with a bill-hook. By morning she has left, and the farm has its geese.

events.text: A brambled cat sits on the well-lid of the abandoned farm, washing a paw. The farmer's son, who knows the place, says she was a house-cat once, and went feral when the family left. He asks if you will bring her back. The cat regards you with sidelong contempt.

choices.text: Tire her out and carry her home

ok.log: It takes the whole afternoon. At the end she lets you pick her up, limp and sullen, and hold her all the way down the lane.

fail.log: She will not be caught. She leaves you with a lap of thorns. (-13 health)

choices.text: Leave a saucer of milk at the well

effects.log: She does not come while you are there. In the morning the saucer is empty.

events.text: The snow-lodge below the pass has been snowed in for a week. At midnight a ferret the size of a horse slips under the door like a river of white fur, circling the sleeping travellers. It does not bite. It looks at each of them, and then, thoughtfully, at the stores.

choices.text: Wake and drive it off

ok.log: It flows under your guard like water. You corner it in the hearth-nook and, after a scramble, hold it down. It looks up at you with black pleading eyes, then flees into the drifts.

fail.log: It knocks you into the woodpile, steals the cheese, and goes. (-18 health)

choices.text: Set out a plate of sausage near the door

ok.log: The ferret takes the sausage, and a long look at the sleeping travellers, and goes back into the snow.

fail.log: It takes the sausage, and the bread. (-9 health)

choices.text: Sit up with the fire and let it prowl

effects.log: It prowls all night. At dawn it has gone, leaving a faint frost pattern across the floor.

events.text: In the high orchard a ferret as big as a pony has been burrowing under the snow, and the trees are dying where it has been. The orchard-keeper stands by the fence, wringing his hands. The ferret emerges for air, white against white, and begins to tunnel again, playful.

choices.text: Drive it out of the orchard

ok.log: It bounds from drift to drift. At last you pin it against the fence, and it squeals and slides under your arm and away over the field.

fail.log: It tunnels beneath you and you fall into its burrow. (-18 health)

choices.text: Show the keeper how to flood the burrows

effects.log: It takes a day of digging. The ferret seems almost pleased to be made to leave.

events.text: The mill-pond has stopped turning the wheel. Something has taken up on the dam: a heron tall as a door, slate blue, with streaks of lightning in the feathers of its neck. Each time the miller waves it off, it spears the sky and brings down a bolt on the millstone.

choices.text: Walk out along the dam and challenge it

ok.log: It strikes at your head. You duck, step in, and take its neck in both hands. It sags, crackling, and flaps away down the valley.

fail.log: The bolt takes you in the chest. You come to in the miller's kitchen with your hair standing on end. (-18 health)

choices.text: Draw the lightning to the iron rod you set on the roof

ok.log: The next bolt runs harmlessly down the rod and into the earth. The heron blinks, outwitted, and leaves.

fail.log: The rod melts. (-9 health)

choices.text: Wait a week for the weather to change

effects.log: The storm breaks eventually, and the heron with it. The mill turns again.

events.text: Fishers on the lake edge say the heron has been standing in the shallows since before they were born. Lately it has been fishing out the carp pond for the thunderstorm it brews inside. The old fisher shrugs. "I've no quarrel with it," he says. "But a man has to eat."

choices.text: Try to make it leave

ok.log: It hardly seems to move, and yet your blows glance off. At last it lifts into the air and goes with a long clap of thunder. The old fisher raises his hat.

fail.log: It stabs you out of the shallows and goes back to fishing. (-18 health)

choices.text: Stock the pond with minnows to keep both fed

effects.log: It takes a week and a sack of minnows. The heron takes to the lake with great content, and never troubles the carp.

events.text: A serpent has threaded itself through the roots of the cider-orchard, thick as a barrel-stave, bark-brown and silent. The pickers found it by its eyes: two amber discs among the roots. The trees are wilting. The pickers refuse to work until it is gone.

choices.text: Dig it out of the roots

ok.log: You wade into the earth and haul it by the neck. It tenses, uncoils, and slides away through a hole in the hedge. The pickers go back to the trees.

fail.log: The roots close around your ankle, and it is a long, humiliating climb out. (-18 health)

choices.text: Pour out a trough of sweet cider as a decoy

ok.log: It follows the smell out of the roots, drinks, and sleeps. You carry it, groggy, to the next valley.

fail.log: It drinks, and bites. (-9 health)

choices.text: Let the pickers work around it

effects.log: They do, nervously, humming. By spring the serpent has moved on.

events.text: The village well has gone bitter. A diver sent down on a rope comes up with a handful of root-fibre and a look of horror. The roots of the old oak have found the well, he says, and something is coiled in them. At the top of the shaft you hear a slow, wet rasp.

choices.text: Go down the shaft after it

ok.log: You descend by rope into the dark and fight it by feel. When you drag it into the daylight, it blinks, a small brown rope with eyes, and the village is silent.

fail.log: It binds you in the roots, and the villagers haul you out by the rope. (-18 health)

choices.text: Cut the oak's roots back from the well

effects.log: It is days of hard labour. The serpent leaves with the roots, and the water clears.

events.text: A boulder on the hill road has been getting bigger. The carters first noticed when a wheel clipped it, and it croaked. A boulder toad, wide as a haywain, grey and lichen-spotted, has settled in the cutting and will not be moved. Traffic is backing up for a mile.

choices.text: Prise it off the road

ok.log: You get a bar under its jaw and heave. It resists, then heaves itself, with a vast offended croak. It leaps into the field and sits, glaring.

fail.log: It squats on you, with the dignity of a hill. (-18 health)

choices.text: Tickle its flank with a reed

ok.log: It shifts, grumbling, and hops aside. The carters cheer, and then fall silent as the shadow of a hop passes over them.

fail.log: It swallows the reed. (-8 health)

choices.text: Dig a bypass round it

effects.log: It takes a week with spades. Then the toad moves on of its own accord.

events.text: Children have discovered that a toad the size of a cottage will croak a song if you strike its back with a stick. The song is low and rich and shakes the pebbles on the road. The toad does not seem to mind. But it has begun to follow the children home.

choices.text: Show the toad it should not follow them

ok.log: You run it back up the hill, a lumbering procession, and wedge it into its cutting. It sits in the rubble, bewildered.

fail.log: It sits on you, in the middle of the road. (-18 health)

choices.text: Teach the children to leave it be

effects.log: They grumble. The toad sulks in its cutting through the winter.

events.text: A hare has been whistling in the night-fields, a thin sweet note that sets the dogs howling and the sheep scattering. The farmers have never seen it; it moves too quickly. Tonight, in the moonlight, you catch a glimpse: long grey ears, a leap that takes it twenty paces, and a whistle like a flute.

choices.text: Match your speed to the hare

ok.log: It leaps and you leap with it. The chase takes you across three fields, and in the end you catch it by the scruff. It looks at you with astonished dark eyes, then whistles, and you hear a hundred answering whistles from the hedge.

fail.log: It leaves you standing in the furrow with your breath ragged. (-18 health)

choices.text: Whistle back and see what answers

ok.log: The hare stops. It tilts its ears at you. For an hour the two of you whistle together across the dark field.

fail.log: You whistle off-key. It is disgusted. (-5 health)

choices.text: Let the farmers stop their ears with wax

effects.log: It is a temporary measure. The hare moves on by the full moon.

events.text: The village goat has been found dancing in the pen, and no one will stop her. The hare crouches on the fence, whistling, ears flicking. The goat leaps with her hooves in the air. All of the village stands around the pen in a ring, half charmed, half uneasy.

choices.text: Seize the hare and end the dance

ok.log: You leap the fence and grab. The hare squeals and bolts. The goat collapses, panting, in a heap.

fail.log: The hare dodges. The goat dances on. (-18 health)

choices.text: Dance along until the tune ends

effects.log: It takes all night. The village joins in, and by dawn the hare has gone, and the whole parish is exhausted and happy.

events.text: A lynx walks the charcoal-burners' hills, coat the colour of grey ash and eyes like embers. Wherever it walks the leaves smoulder faintly. The charcoal-burners swear that their kilns burn hotter where it passes, and that their dogs will not go near it. It watches them work, from the ridge.

choices.text: Stalk the lynx along the ridge

ok.log: It leaps from rock to rock, trailing sparks, and you follow. At the end of the ridge you catch it in a ring of fern. It snarls, then goes still, and the smouldering stops.

fail.log: It leaves you with a burned hand and an empty ridge. (-18 health)

choices.text: Dowse the kiln-edge to keep the forest safe

ok.log: The lynx circles all night but the leaves do not catch. Before dawn it has gone.

fail.log: The wind shifts and the leaves catch. (-8 health)

choices.text: Leave the burners to cope with it

effects.log: They do, though the smell of scorched fur lingers for days.

events.text: A scorched pawprint lies on the doorstep of the charcoal-burner's cottage, each toe-mark glowing faintly. The burner's wife has found them in the garden too, across the washing, across the ladder. The lynx has not harmed them, but the thatch is smouldering where it passes.

choices.text: Wait up and face the lynx at the door

ok.log: It comes at midnight, a streak of grey ash. You hold the doorway until it lies panting on the step, and then it goes, with a flick of its tail.

fail.log: It pads past you into the thatch, and you spend the night with a bucket. (-18 health)

choices.text: Wet the thatch and leave out a dish of ash

effects.log: The lynx sniffs the ash, and rolls in it, and goes. The burner's wife thinks you a wizard.

events.text: The deep well of the market-square has begun to gurgle at night. A long grey eel the thickness of a rope has taken up in it, and now it surfaces at dusk to look at passers-by with one cold, patient eye. The water has turned sweet and strangely heavy. The market-women have stopped drawing it.

choices.text: Lower yourself down the shaft and take the eel on

ok.log: It strikes at you in the dark, cold as a river. You grip it behind the head and haul. It slips free, but it is gone, and the water runs clear.

fail.log: It wraps you in its coils and you are drawn up half drowned. (-18 health)

choices.text: Lower a basket of worms to draw it up

ok.log: It rises to the basket, eats, and is lifted out. You carry it in a barrel to the river.

fail.log: It takes the basket and the rope. (-8 health)

choices.text: Draw from the other wells until it leaves

effects.log: It takes a month. One morning the water is clear again.

events.text: An old man says the well eel is his grandfather's eel. His grandfather put it in the well to keep it clean, and it has lived there ever since. Now the old man is dying, and he asks you, in a thin voice, to see that it is looked after.

choices.text: Test the eel, to see if it can be trusted

ok.log: It fights you gently, and clearly knows its limits. The old man, watching from the doorway, nods.

fail.log: It slaps you across the face with its tail, as if in reproach. (-18 health)

choices.text: Promise the old man you will look after it

effects.log: You promise. You do, too, and some nights you sit by the well and listen to the slow splash of a long patient life.

events.text: Where your world was first dreamed there is a hollow in the hills that no map shows, and in it, outlined in mist, sleeps the First Beast. It has the shape of a wolf, and an elk, and a bear, and a bird, all at once, and none of them. It is the oldest thing here. It is the only thing that remembers being thought of.

choices.text: Ask the First Beast for the honour of a bout

ok.log: You fight in a hollow that has no edges. At the end it lowers its head to you, and in that moment you remember something you have forgotten, and then you forget it again.

fail.log: It is gentle with you, by its standards. You wake a day later on the hillside, alive and humbled, and the hollow is gone. (-35 health)

choices.text: Sit at the edge of the hollow and keep it company

effects.log: You sit until the stars come out, and the First Beast stirs. The world feels bigger for having it in it.

events.text: Every child in the world has had the same dream once: a huge soft shape moving in the dark, calling their name. The First Beast is that dream, and tonight it stands before the lantern-light of a lonely farmhouse, waiting. The farmer's family watches from the window, hand in hand. The beast looks at you, and its eyes are very old.

choices.text: Step out and meet the dream

ok.log: You cross the yard to it. The fight is quiet and slow and strange, and at the end it breathes in your face and you hear, for an instant, the whole world singing.

fail.log: The dream sweeps over you, and when you wake it is morning and the beast is gone. (-35 health)

choices.text: Stay in the doorway and let it look its fill

effects.log: It looks at the farmhouse for a long time, and then at the stars. Then it turns, and walks away over the field, and the grass springs up behind it.
